subject: general
concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
question: Which of the following statements regarding the estimation of India’s national and per capita income during the colonial rule is correct?

options.text: The colonial government never made any sincere attempt to estimate India’s national and per capita income.
The colonial government estimated India’s national and per capita income sincerely every year.
The colonial government estimated India’s per capita income but ignored national income.
The colonial government estimated India’s national income but ignored per capita income.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The colonial government never made any sincere attempt to estimate India's national and per capita income.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The colonial government showed very little interest in understanding the **economic conditions of India**. They were more focused on exploiting resources and maintaining control rather than conducting comprehensive studies on India's economic data.
 
• There was no systematic or sincere effort to estimate India's **national income** or **per capita income**. Most of the work done on these topics was initiated by Indian economists and scholars during the late colonial period.
 
• Indian economists like **Dadabhai Naoroji** made efforts to calculate India's national income during colonial rule. His work, though pioneering, was not supported by the colonial government. *Hence, the colonial government did not estimate India's income sincerely.*
 
• Statement 2 is incorrect because the colonial government never undertook annual calculations of India's national and per capita income.
 
• Statement 3 is incorrect as the colonial government did not focus on estimating per capita income, either. The economic well-being of the Indian population was not among their priorities.
 
• Statement 4 is also incorrect because neither the national income nor the per capita income of India was systematically estimated by the colonial government.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is The colonial government never made any sincere attempt to estimate India's national and per capita income..***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Economic Exploitation during Colonial Rule:**

 
 
• The British colonial government prioritized resource extraction and economic exploitation over addressing the welfare of the Indian population.
 
• India's wealth was systematically drained through policies like the **Drain Theory**, elaborated by Dadabhai Naoroji in his book **"Poverty and Un-British Rule in India"**.
 
 
 
• **Efforts by Indian Economists:**
 
 
• Indian economists like **Dadabhai Naoroji**, **R.C. Desai**, and **William Digby** made attempts to estimate India's income during colonial rule.
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji** used available data to calculate India's national income and highlighted the impoverishment caused by British policies.
 
 
 
• **Impact of British Policies:**
 
 
• The lack of income data made it difficult to assess the true impact of British policies, but the visible effects included widespread **poverty**, **famine**, and **economic stagnation**.
 
• The absence of reliable income statistics also hindered efforts to plan for economic recovery post-Independence.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Characteristics of Colonial Economic Policies:**

 
 
• Focus on resource extraction, such as raw materials for British industries (e.g., cotton, jute).
 
• Neglect of infrastructure development for Indian welfare, with investments mainly for British commercial interests (railways, ports).
 
 
 
• **Significance of National Income Estimation:**
 
 
• Estimation of national and per capita income is crucial for understanding the economic health of a country and planning policies for development.
 
• Post-Independence, India began systematic efforts to estimate national income through organizations like the **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)** and **Central Statistical Organization (CSO)**.
